themes.name: Fast Food Leader
themes.description: Dominant players in the quick-service restaurant industry focusing on rapid customer service, standardized menus, and efficient kitchen operations to serve meals quickly.

linked_companies.name: MC DONALD'S-CORP
linked_companies.description: Operates an extensive global network of franchised and company-owned quick-service restaurants, driving industry standards through operational efficiency, standardized menu offerings, and immense scale.
linked_companies.evidence: McDonald's operates as a pure-play quick-service restaurant (QSR) operator, securing its fast-food leadership by capturing market share across nearly all top international markets and driving a 6% increase in global system-wide sales in the recent quarter. To further cement its market position, which includes a mid-40% global market share in beef, C-level executives are executing an aggressive strategy to expand the brand's footprint to 50,000 global locations by 2027. This physical expansion is directly supported by multibillion-dollar capital investments designed to standardize global technology platforms, maximize drive-thru capabilities, and deploy speed-of-service initiatives like "Ready on Arrival" to ensure rapid kitchen-to-customer execution.

linked_companies.name: YUM! BRANDS INC
linked_companies.description: Operates and franchises a comprehensive global portfolio of quick-service restaurant brands, including KFC, Taco Bell, and Pizza Hut, driving widespread scale and market penetration across the fast-food industry.
linked_companies.evidence: Yum! Brands' foundational identity in the quick-service restaurant (QSR) industry is driven by its flagship portfolio of global category leaders, primarily KFC and Taco Bell, which collectively generate the vast majority of the company's operating profit across over 60,000 worldwide locations. The company continually reinforces this competitive moat through superior operational metrics, highlighted recently by Taco Bell achieving the fastest drive-thru times among large-scale QSR players and delivering eight consecutive quarters of above-industry same-store sales growth. To sustain this extensive global footprint across 155 countries, the organization has deeply embedded QSR innovation into its corporate structure by deploying dedicated executive roles, including a Global Chief Concept Officer and a Chief Scale Officer, to optimize its supply chain and drive worldwide franchise expansion.

linked_companies.name: DOMINO'S PIZZA INC
linked_companies.description: Operates a global network of franchised and company-owned pizza delivery and carryout restaurants, leveraging proprietary digital ordering platforms and integrated supply chain facilities to drive quick-service food operations worldwide.
linked_companies.evidence: Domino's operates as the market leader in the Quick-Service Restaurant (QSR) pizza segment, driven by the capture of 11 points of U.S. market share over the past 11 years and securing 33 percent of the pizza delivery market. The company fuels this expansion using an advertising budget equal to its top two competitors combined, alongside operational technologies like the DomOS orchestration agent for efficient, just-in-time pizza making. Supporting its position as the world's largest pizza company, Domino's maintains over 22,300 global locations and ranks first in net store growth among traditional public QSR brands with over 3,000 units. As a pure-play fast food entity, the organization is dedicating its $120 million capital expenditure budget in 2026 to open nearly 1,000 net new stores worldwide and continuously acquire market share from national competitors.

linked_companies.name: WENDY'S CO/THE
linked_companies.description: Operates and franchises an extensive global network of quick-service restaurants, shaping the fast food industry through signature made-to-order menu items, drive-thru efficiency, and expanding digital and delivery channels.
linked_companies.evidence: Wendy's alignment with the Fast Food Leader theme is driven by its pure-play quick-service restaurant (QSR) business model, which generates its entire revenue base from fast-food operations. To solidify its competitive positioning as the highest-quality choice among QSR burger chains, the company is executing its Project Fresh turnaround strategy under the direction of its interim CEO. This strategy is backed by a budgeted $120 million to $130 million in annual capital expenditures targeted at digital integration, system footprint optimization, and its proprietary fresh never frozen beef supply chain. Furthermore, Wendy's anchors its market dominance as the second-largest U.S. and third-largest global hamburger chain by traffic and dollar share, continuously expanding its field operations workforce to ensure standardized, rapid service.

linked_companies.name: YUM CHINA HOLDINGS INC
linked_companies.description: Functions as a major operator of quick-service restaurant chains, driving the fast-food sector through extensive brand expansion, digital integration, and high-volume operations across a vast consumer market.
linked_companies.evidence: Yum China operates as the largest quick-service restaurant (QSR) company in China, anchored by its flagship KFC brand, which holds an exclusive licensing moat and managed 13,454 locations across more than 2,600 cities as of Q1 2026. This fast-food division acts as the company's primary financial engine, generating $2.45 billion—approximately 75% of total consolidated revenue—in the first quarter of 2026 alone. To sustain this market position, the company leverages a dedicated organizational structure for its 11,317 company-owned KFC units and allocates the bulk of its $600 million to $700 million projected 2026 capital expenditures toward network expansion and store remodeling. The current growth strategy builds directly on momentum from late 2025, where the company utilized a specialized management structure to outpace the broader Chinese restaurant industry in system sales growth.

themes.name: Restaurant Expansion
themes.description: Growth strategies involving franchising, opening new locations, and enhancing service models to widen reach and increase customer base in the hospitality sector.

linked_companies.name: WINGSTOP INC
linked_companies.description: Drives rapid unit growth by continuously developing and opening new franchised and company-owned locations to scale its domestic and international footprint.
linked_companies.evidence: Wingstop's engagement with restaurant expansion is anchored by its explicit long-term objective to scale its physical footprint to over 10,000 locations globally. Advancing this strategy in the second quarter of 2026, the company opened 97 net new restaurants to achieve a 17% unit growth rate, keeping it on track for a 15% to 16% full-year global unit growth target. The buildout is secured by a pipeline of over 2,200 restaurant commitments and involves active penetration into new international markets such as Ireland, Thailand, and India. This continuous physical scaling directly fuels Wingstop's top-line performance, with expansion-driven franchise fees and royalties generating $87.5 million of its $183.7 million total quarterly revenue.

linked_companies.name: MC DONALD'S-CORP
linked_companies.description: Drives global restaurant expansion by continuously developing and opening new franchised and company-operated locations to scale its worldwide footprint and increase market penetration.
linked_companies.evidence: McDonald's functionally embeds restaurant expansion into its "Accelerating the Arches" strategy by designating "Restaurant Development" as a core growth pillar overseen by dedicated global senior leadership. To drive the fastest period of unit growth in company history, management is allocating the majority of its $3.7 billion to $3.9 billion 2026 capital expenditure budget toward opening approximately 2,600 new locations globally this year. This physical real estate build-out demands extensive global workforce scaling, highlighted by targeted talent development efforts in China to support over 1,000 new regional additions. This ongoing expansion pipeline keeps McDonald's on track to reach 50,000 total restaurants by the end of 2027, with net new units projected to drive approximately 2.5% of 2026 system-wide sales growth.

linked_companies.name: YUM! BRANDS INC
linked_companies.description: Drives global restaurant expansion by leveraging a franchise-focused business model to continuously open new quick-service locations and scale its diverse brand portfolio across international markets.
linked_companies.evidence: Yum! Brands drives its long-term growth algorithm through global unit development, highlighted by 4,550 new unit openings over the past year and a corporate target of exceeding 5% net new unit growth. Evidence from the first quarter of 2026 emphasizes this strategy, as KFC achieved its 30,000th international restaurant and Taco Bell advanced its goal to reach 10,000 North American and 3,000 international units by 2030. To execute this footprint expansion, leadership deployed analytics-driven store development teams, appointed a Chief Scale Officer, and allocated capital specifically for growth, including a $668 million acquisition of 128 Taco Bell locations. This continual expansion directly fuels financial performance, with new unit growth explicitly contributing 3% to the company's 5% quarterly system sales increase.

linked_companies.name: WENDY'S CO/THE
linked_companies.description: Drives global footprint growth by opening new quick-service restaurant locations and leveraging franchise development agreements across domestic and international markets.
linked_companies.evidence: Wendy's executes restaurant expansion as a central component of its growth strategy, anchored by a recent agreement to build up to 1,000 new franchise locations across China over the next ten years. The company supports this global footprint scaling by deploying a 'future fresh' restaurant design and utilizing on-the-ground regional leadership teams, generating a 6% increase in international system-wide sales through net unit additions in Mexico and the Philippines. Capital allocation aligns directly with this physical development mandate, evidenced by $9.1 million directed toward build-to-suit initiatives in the first quarter, while the domestic strategy temporarily sequences new unit construction behind average unit volume (AUV) optimization.

linked_companies.name: CAVA GROUP INC
linked_companies.description: Focuses on scaling its physical footprint by opening new restaurant locations and entering additional geographic markets to drive overall growth.
linked_companies.evidence: CAVA identifies restaurant expansion as its first strategic pillar, opening 20 net new locations in early 2026 to achieve a 20.2% year-over-year unit base increase. Directing its cash reserves toward unit growth rather than external acquisitions, the company targets 75 to 77 new store openings for the full year and estimates preopening costs up to $22.5 million to support entry into markets like Ohio, Missouri, and Minnesota. To manage this footprint expansion and progress toward a stated goal of 1,000 locations by 2032, management restructured field operations under a new Chief Operations Officer, formed an internal real estate team, and launched the 'Flavor Your Future' training initiative to develop an Assistant General Manager leadership pipeline. These newly scaled locations, which feature the updated 'Project Soul' physical format, achieve average unit volumes exceeding $3 million and drive the divergence between the company's total revenue growth and its same-restaurant sales metrics.

themes.name: E-Commerce
themes.description: Conducting retail, services, and transactions via electronic platforms, harnessing digital and internet technologies to facilitate shopping, banking, and information dissemination.

linked_companies.name: COUPANG INC
linked_companies.description: Operates a comprehensive e-commerce platform supported by an integrated, end-to-end logistics network that enables rapid fulfillment and delivery of a vast selection of consumer goods.
linked_companies.evidence: Coupang operates primarily as a pure-play e-commerce enterprise, structured around its core Product Commerce segment, which most recently delivered $7.2 billion of the company's $8.5 billion consolidated net revenues. The company directs billions of dollars in capital expenditures into a proprietary logistics network, equipping dedicated teams to manage online retail operations and fulfillment infrastructure. To capture further market share and serve nearly 24 million active customers, Coupang scales its e-commerce ecosystem by integrating a first-party retail catalog with a faster-growing third-party marketplace powered by Fulfillment and Logistics by Coupang (FLC).

linked_companies.name: EBAY INC
linked_companies.description: Operates a global online marketplace connecting buyers and sellers, facilitating digital retail through consumer-to-consumer and business-to-consumer transactions across both auction-style and fixed-price formats.
linked_companies.evidence: eBay operates as a pure-play global digital marketplace, with its core e-commerce infrastructure driving $3.09 billion in quarterly revenue and over $22.2 billion in gross merchandise volume. The company's organizational framework, led directly by its C-suite executives, is strictly designed to facilitate digital transactions for 136 million active buyers across more than 2.5 billion active listings. To scale this ecosystem and consistently outpace industry benchmarks, eBay dedicates 4% to 5% of its corporate revenue to capital expenditures while actively executing strategic platform acquisitions, such as the $1.2 billion purchase of Depop, to expand its consumer-to-consumer capabilities.

linked_companies.name: AMAZON.COM INC
linked_companies.description: Operates a global online retail marketplace that connects consumers with a vast selection of proprietary and third-party merchandise, supported by an extensive fulfillment and logistics infrastructure.
linked_companies.evidence: Amazon's organizational identity is fundamentally defined by its e-commerce business, which generated $143.9 billion across its North America and International segments in the second quarter of 2026, capturing nearly 80% of total revenue. This retail engine is driven by a 15% year-over-year increase in store units and a vast third-party marketplace, which recently expanded through global fee reductions and the deployment of AI-generated custom data visualizations in Seller Central. To sustain its operational scale and support millions of merchants, the company continuously directs multi-billion-dollar investments into supply chain improvements, large-format fulfillment centers, and artificial intelligence shopping tools like Rufus. These capacity enhancements, combined with ultra-fast delivery options and massive shopping events like Prime Day and the Big Spring Sale, establish a deeply integrated retail network that seamlessly connects consumers and third-party sellers.

linked_companies.name: CHEWY INC - CLASS A
linked_companies.description: Operates a specialized digital retail platform for pet products and pharmacy services, advancing the e-commerce sector through direct-to-consumer fulfillment and automated subscription deliveries.
linked_companies.evidence: Chewy operates exclusively as a pure-play e-commerce platform, generating its entire $3.36 billion in recent quarterly net sales through retail websites and mobile applications. Positioning itself as the largest pet e-tailer in the United States, the company serves 21.5 million active customers and drives revenue consistency through its digital Autoship subscription program, which accounts for 84.4% of total sales. The company's organizational framework is entirely dedicated to supporting this online marketplace, utilizing large-scale fulfillment centers, digital bidding algorithms, and dedicated technologists to manage a highly scalable tech stack. Additionally, strategic financial allocations, such as $129.2 million in annual capital expenditures and the $175 million acquisition of SmartPak, are fundamentally designed to expand its e-commerce infrastructure and capitalize on secular shifts toward online consumer purchasing.

linked_companies.name: WAYFAIR INC- CLASS A
linked_companies.description: Operates a dedicated e-commerce platform focused on furniture and home goods, providing consumers with digital retail access to a vast selection of products from numerous global suppliers.
linked_companies.evidence: Wayfair operates as a pure-play digital marketplace, utilizing its primary platform, Wayfair.com, to connect home goods suppliers directly with retail consumers. This e-commerce infrastructure relies on a centralized technology organization of over 2,000 engineers and data scientists managing an online catalog of 40 million products. To maintain this digital-first retail delivery mechanism, the company routinely allocates capital expenditures, including $54 million in a recent quarter, toward global tech replatforming and native mobile applications. By functioning as an inventory-light platform that leverages supplier competition to optimize retail prices, Wayfair captures nearly the entirety of its revenue through digital transactions.

themes.name: Loyalty Programs
themes.description: Marketing initiatives designed to reward repeat customers and foster brand loyalty.

linked_companies.name: COSTCO WHOLESALE CORP
linked_companies.description: Operates a subscription-based warehouse club model that functions as a core loyalty program, driving high customer retention and recurring revenue through exclusive member access to discounted merchandise and services.
linked_companies.evidence: Costco's business model is fundamentally structured around its exclusive paid membership program, which serves as the primary profit engine for the company. By Q2 2026, the retailer reported 82.9 million total paid members and $1.373 billion in membership fee income, supported by an entrenched 92.2 percent renewal rate in the U.S. and Canada. The company's strategic focus centers on retaining these members and encouraging upgrades to the 41.2 million-strong Executive tier, which provides exclusive rewards and dictates the retailer's broader trajectory. To further incentivize higher-tier upgrades, Costco leverages targeted marketing partnerships and retention strategies, such as offering member credits, to solidify the subscription loop at the core of its operations.

linked_companies.name: DELTA AIR LINES INC.
linked_companies.description: Operates a comprehensive frequent flyer program that incentivizes customer retention and generates substantial ancillary revenue through tiered rewards and strategic co-branded credit card partnerships.
linked_companies.evidence: Delta engages with Loyalty Programs through its SkyMiles ecosystem and an exclusive co-branded credit card partnership with American Express, which recently generated over $2 billion in quarterly remuneration driven by a 12% increase in cardholder spend. The company actively expands this ecosystem's utility beyond air travel by dedicating specific executive leadership to the division and integrating rewards with partners like Uber, connecting over 1.5 million user accounts. These loyalty initiatives operate as an engine of enterprise value that fuels high-margin commercial growth, delivering over $8.2 billion in annual partner remuneration and accounting for more than 14% of Delta's total operating revenue.

linked_companies.name: AMERICAN AIRLINES GROUP INC
linked_companies.description: Drives customer retention and ancillary revenue through its AAdvantage frequent flyer program, leveraging co-branded credit card partnerships and tiered rewards to incentivize repeat travel.
linked_companies.evidence: American Airlines positions its AAdvantage program as the largest airline loyalty program globally and designates 'leading in loyalty' as one of its four core strategic pillars. Supported by digital investments like a redesigned mobile app and an exclusive 10-year co-branded credit card partnership with Citi, the program achieved a 25% year-over-year increase in enrollments during the second quarter of 2026. This growing member base drives the majority of the airline's premium and flown revenue, generating approximately $1 billion in quarterly marketing remuneration and producing billions in partner cash payments under the oversight of a dedicated commercial leadership team.

linked_companies.name: AMERICAN EXPRESS CO
linked_companies.description: Operates a proprietary Membership Rewards platform and extensive co-branded credit card partnerships that incentivize cardmember spending and drive long-term customer retention.
linked_companies.evidence: American Express integrates loyalty directly into its foundational business strategy through its overarching Membership Model and flagship Membership Rewards program. Underscoring this commitment in early 2026, the company reported a $6.3 billion annual investment toward marketing and rewards generation, sustaining an exceptional 97 percent Ultimate Redemption Rate among participants. This rewards ecosystem is further expanded by extensive international co-brand partnerships—including British Airways and ANA—and a dedicated loyalty coalition business within its International Card Services segment that generates hundreds of millions in targeted service fees. Ultimately, these integrated rewards platforms function as the core value proposition driving customer acquisition, premium cardholder retention, and multi-generational spending across the company's product lines.

linked_companies.name: MARRIOTT INTERNATIONAL -CL A
linked_companies.description: Operates a comprehensive global rewards program that incentivizes repeat bookings and customer retention by offering members points, exclusive benefits, and personalized experiences across a vast portfolio of hotel brands.
linked_companies.evidence: Marriott Bonvoy functions as the core retention engine for the company's lodging ecosystem, expanding its user base to nearly 283 million members globally by the second quarter of 2026. The program actively drives direct bookings and repeat stays, utilizing an expansive network of 37 co-branded credit cards across 13 countries following recent launches in Indonesia and Brazil. Structurally embedded within the company's operations, the loyalty platform commands an $8.19 billion program liability and constitutes a primary pillar of a $350 million to $440 million digital technology transformation budget.

themes.name: Agribusiness
themes.description: Encompasses all aspects of agriculture, from crop and livestock production to processing and distribution, integrating technology and sustainability practices to maximize productivity and market reach.

linked_companies.name: CORTEVA INC
linked_companies.description: Provides a comprehensive portfolio of advanced seed genetics, crop protection products, and digital agronomic solutions designed to enhance global agricultural productivity and support sustainable farming operations.
linked_companies.evidence: Corteva functions entirely as an agribusiness pure-play, highlighted by an ongoing restructuring led by CEO Charles Magro to divide its 22,000-employee workforce into two specialized entities: a Crop Protection business and a newly established advanced seed and genetics company named Vylor. The company's comprehensive grip on global farming inputs is anchored by its century-old Pioneer brand, leading corn market share in Brazil, and an extensive out-licensing network for its proprietary Enlist seed traits. Corteva aggressively expands this footprint through strategic capital deployment, most recently executing a $700 million payout for Bayer crop technology and launching a Latin American biofuels joint venture with BP. Furthermore, the company sustains its vast agricultural ecosystem through structural farmer support, dedicating over $1 billion annually to agricultural R&D and funding a nearly $1 billion crop-and-seed barter program to mitigate financial risks for growers.

linked_companies.name: ARCHER-DANIELS-MIDLAND CO
linked_companies.description: Procures, transports, stores, and processes agricultural commodities into food, feed, and industrial products, operating as a foundational global supply chain link between farmers and consumers.
linked_companies.evidence: ADM operates as an essential global agricultural supply chain manager and processor, with agribusiness directly driving its entire organizational structure and all of its operating profit across the Ag Services and Oilseeds, Carbohydrate Solutions, and Nutrition segments. The company controls an end-to-end value chain spanning crop origination, grain export logistics, oilseed crushing, and specialized ingredient processing, sustained by a total corporate capital expenditure budget of $1.3 billion to $1.5 billion. Expanding this integrated footprint, ADM recently achieved record global site crush production and structurally grew its animal nutrition division by contributing physical feed mills to a joint venture with Alltech.

linked_companies.name: BUNGE GLOBAL SA
linked_companies.description: Operates a comprehensive agricultural supply chain network dedicated to sourcing, processing, and distributing oilseeds, grains, and related commodities for global food, animal feed, and biofuel markets.
linked_companies.evidence: Bunge's core organizational structure revolves around an integrated global agribusiness platform managing the complete crop lifecycle across origination, merchandising, processing, and distribution. Through its integration with Viterra, the company expanded its end-to-end value chain operating model, establishing itself as the biggest agricultural business in Argentina and extending its reach to touch more farmers globally than any other entity. The company derives all of its core segment earnings from these agricultural activities, sustaining this market position with a full-year 2026 capital expenditure budget of $1.5 billion to $1.7 billion aimed at growth and productivity.

linked_companies.name: MOSAIC CO/THE
linked_companies.description: Focuses on the production and distribution of concentrated phosphate and potash crop nutrients, supplying essential fertilizers to enhance global agricultural yields and support broad farming operations.
linked_companies.evidence: Mosaic's integration into the agribusiness sector is driven by its position as an end-to-end supplier of crop nutrients, livestock feed ingredients like dicalcium phosphate, and global distribution logistics. The company's operations are intertwined with agricultural market conditions, demonstrated by a $1.25 billion capital expenditure budget directed at crop supply chains and fertilizer production networks. Organizationally, this alignment is formalized through dedicated executive leadership and the Mosaic Fertilizantes segment, which actively manages localized seasonal demand and farmer credit risks in South America. The company also continually scales its agribusiness infrastructure through physical capacity expansions, such as the completion of a 1 million tonne crop nutrient blending facility in Palmeirante to supply fast-growing agricultural regions in Brazil.

linked_companies.name: DEERE & CO
linked_companies.description: Manufactures a comprehensive portfolio of agricultural equipment, including tractors, harvesters, and precision farming technologies, that optimize crop production and streamline farm management operations globally.
linked_companies.evidence: Deere & Company functions as a foundational equipment and technology provider for the global agribusiness sector, organizing its core operations around its Production & Precision Agriculture and Small Agriculture & Turf segments. During Q2 2026, these agricultural divisions generated nearly $8 billion in combined revenue—comprising nearly 60% of total net sales—by supplying essential machinery and solutions to crop, dairy, and livestock producers. To continually align with the agricultural market business cycle, Deere is directing a $20 billion, 10-year capital investment into U.S. manufacturing to maximize agricultural productivity, alongside expanding its global footprint with 20 new machinery models recently introduced in key markets such as Brazil.

themes.name: Precision Agriculture
themes.description: Farming management concept using advanced technology like sensors, GPS mapping, and data analytics to monitor field variability and optimize crop production practices based on site-specific needs.

linked_companies.name: DEERE & CO
linked_companies.description: Integrates advanced automation, GPS guidance, and data analytics into agricultural machinery to optimize crop yields, improve resource efficiency, and drive the adoption of smart farming practices.
linked_companies.evidence: Deere's engagement with Precision Agriculture is driven by its dedicated Production and Precision Ag segment, which generated $4.5 billion in recent quarterly net sales to account for approximately a third of total revenue. The segment develops and integrates proprietary technologies into farming equipment, including ExactDepth for furrow optimization, ExactShot for automated fertilizer placement, and See & Spray camera platforms. These hardware solutions are centrally managed through the John Deere Operations Center, an agricultural technology platform hosting nearly 440,000 monthly active users. The deployment of these capabilities is evidenced by a 99 percent attachment rate for harvest automation on recent combine orders, reflecting the ongoing integration of precision automation into production-scale farming operations.

linked_companies.name: LINDSAY CORP
linked_companies.description: Manufactures automated center pivot irrigation systems and proprietary remote management technologies that enable growers to precisely monitor, control, and optimize water and energy usage across agricultural operations.
linked_companies.evidence: Lindsay Corporation engages with precision agriculture through its dedicated Irrigation segment, which focuses on manufacturing GPS positioning, variable rate irrigation, and remote management technologies. The company enables resource optimization and site-specific field management through proprietary solutions like FieldNET and the Smart Pivot platform's TowerWatch, allowing growers to manage energy and water consumption while performing localized machine diagnostics. Furthermore, the direct integration of these data-driven scheduling and diagnostic capabilities into physical hardware supports the execution of large-scale international agricultural projects, as demonstrated by recent multi-year supply agreements in the MENA region.

linked_companies.name: CNH INDUSTRIAL NV
linked_companies.description: Integrates advanced automation, digital solutions, and precision farming technologies across its agricultural machinery portfolio to optimize crop yields and enhance operational efficiency for growers.
linked_companies.evidence: CNH's engagement with Precision Agriculture is anchored by its strategic prioritization of investments in 'Precision Technology' for its agricultural operations. During Q1 2026, management explicitly maintained R&D funding for these advanced farming concepts despite navigating a cyclical downturn in broader agriculture equipment demand. While technological advancement remains a stated organizational focus alongside cost-reduction initiatives, the company has not yet isolated specific capital expenditures, dedicated headcounts, or commercial product revenues tied directly to these precision agriculture efforts.

linked_companies.name: VALMONT INDUSTRIES
linked_companies.description: Provides advanced precision irrigation equipment and connected crop management technologies, integrating smart center pivots, telemetry, and AI-driven analytics to optimize water efficiency and maximize agricultural yields.
linked_companies.evidence: Valmont engages in Precision Agriculture primarily through its Valley Tech suite, which features the ICON+ control panel and the AgSense 365 platform. These proprietary tools utilize predictive analytics and remote monitoring to provide data-driven irrigation management, enabling farmers to connect machines across brands and optimize crop production. In Q4 2025, these specific technology products and services generated $94.5 million in net sales, supported by dedicated global technical teams and expanding recurring revenues from AgSense. Concurrent with focusing on these core hardware and software offerings, Valmont refined its precision agriculture strategy by exiting its Prospera subsidiary, resulting in a $17.3 million impairment and reduced research and development costs.

linked_companies.name: TRIMBLE INC
linked_companies.description: Delivers specialized positioning technologies, automated steering systems, and comprehensive farm management software designed to optimize crop yields, enhance resource efficiency, and streamline agricultural operations.
linked_companies.evidence: Trimble's engagement with Precision Agriculture centers on the $1.9 billion divestiture of its dedicated agriculture business to AGCO to form the PTx Trimble joint venture. Through this transaction, Trimble transitioned to a non-controlling partner, retaining a 15% equity stake in the joint venture valued at $275.6 million. Despite divesting the core segment, the company retained proprietary GNSS positioning and guidance technologies to continue supporting advanced electronic control products for the mixed-fleet agriculture market.

themes.description: Machines and equipment used in the production environment for manufacturing, assembling, or processing industrial materials and goods.

linked_companies.name: CATERPILLAR INC
linked_companies.description: Manufactures and distributes a comprehensive portfolio of heavy industrial machinery, including construction and mining equipment, diesel engines, and industrial gas turbines that support global infrastructure and resource extraction.
linked_companies.evidence: Caterpillar operates primarily as an industrial machinery manufacturer, generating $17.4 billion in total consolidated sales during the second quarter of 2026 across its Construction, Resource, and Power and Energy divisions. Sales growth within these primary reporting structures is driven by high volumes of heavy equipment and industrial engines distributed across diverse applications, alongside targeted offerings like the Cat Compact line for small contractors. The company's foundational focus on machinery production is further evidenced by a globally connected fleet of over 1.6 million assets and a record $63 billion equipment backlog, reflecting sustained global demand for its heavy industrial systems.

linked_companies.name: FLOWSERVE CORP
linked_companies.description: Manufactures and services critical flow control equipment, including engineered pumps, valves, and mechanical seals, providing foundational industrial machinery for fluid motion and control across the energy, chemical, and water management sectors.
linked_companies.evidence: Flowserve operates as a pure-play manufacturer of precision-engineered flow control equipment, with its organizational structure completely anchored around producing complex industrial machinery. The company's two primary segments, the Flowserve Pump Division (FPD) and the Flow Control Division (FCD), generate nearly all of its $1.1 billion quarterly revenue by designing and distributing highly customized pumps, valves, and mechanical seals. To support these core operations, Flowserve leverages a dedicated workforce of 16,000 employees across 85 global manufacturing facilities, securing its position as the second-largest industrial valve supplier globally. The company is actively expanding its hardware flow-control output through strategic investments, utilizing up to $100 million in 2026 capital expenditures and executing the integration of Trillium Valves, which is projected to add 300 basis points to total sales growth.

linked_companies.name: INGERSOLL-RAND INC
linked_companies.description: Designs and manufactures a comprehensive portfolio of mission-critical air, fluid, and energy technologies, including compressors, pumps, and blowers, that serve as essential industrial machinery across diverse commercial and industrial applications.
linked_companies.evidence: Ingersoll Rand functions as an original equipment manufacturer of heavy industrial machinery, with production hardware like compressors, blowers, and vacuum systems serving as its primary commercial identity. Compressors alone account for upwards of 65% of the company's revenue base, dictating overall organic growth and margins across global operations. The company continuously expands its flow creation portfolio through targeted capital deployments, demonstrated by the recent Q2 2026 acquisition of Fox s.r.l. to add hydropneumatic accumulators to its pump equipment lines. Furthermore, this extensive deployment of original machinery establishes a deeply installed hardware base, driving recurring aftermarket service revenues that constitute 40% of the total business.

linked_companies.name: GRACO INC
linked_companies.description: Manufactures specialized fluid and powder handling machinery, including pumps, sprayers, and dispensing systems, which are utilized across diverse manufacturing, processing, and construction applications.
linked_companies.evidence: Graco designs and manufactures complex industrial machinery through a dedicated Industrial division that provides specialized fluid handling, powder coating, and sealant equipment requiring extensive factory integration. These industrial operations comprise roughly 50% of the company's total revenue, acting as a core business pillar that achieves a 32% operating margin and relies on customized direct-system orders requiring half-cost down payments with virtually zero cancellations. To expand this manufacturing footprint, Graco is currently executing $90 million to $100 million in annual capital expenditures—including $50 million specifically allocated for facility expansion—alongside an inorganic growth strategy featuring recent equipment acquisitions like COROB, Color Service, and Radia. The company's capability in industrial systems is further reinforced by a dedicated product R&D budget, a $40 million proprietary patent portfolio, and the consolidated 'One Graco' operating model.

linked_companies.name: DEERE & CO
linked_companies.description: Manufactures and distributes a comprehensive range of heavy equipment for the agricultural, construction, and forestry sectors, driving the industrial machinery market through the integration of precision technology and automated systems.
linked_companies.evidence: Deere functions primarily as a manufacturer of heavy machinery, generating 88.1% of its total quarterly revenue through the production of agricultural, construction, turf, and forestry equipment. The company's operations encompass capital-intensive segments, including a dedicated Construction and Forestry division that produces earthmoving and road building machines, contributing $3.79 billion in quarterly sales. To further expand its domestic industrial equipment production, Deere recently invested $70 million in a Kernersville, North Carolina facility to manufacture new Deere-designed excavators.

themes.name: Precious Metals
themes.description: Rare, naturally occurring metallic elements with high economic value, such as gold, silver, and platinum, used in jewelry, investment, and industrial applications.

linked_companies.name: NEWMONT CORP
linked_companies.description: Engages in the extensive exploration, extraction, and processing of gold, silver, and other precious metals across a global portfolio of mining assets, serving as a primary supplier of these commodities to the market.
linked_companies.evidence: Newmont operates primarily around precious metals extraction, generating 1.3 million ounces of gold and 9 million ounces of silver during the first quarter of 2026. Guided by operations across Cadia, Yanacocha, and Peñasquito, the company maintains the industry's largest gold reserves and officially ranks as the world's third-largest silver producer. Gold and silver outputs drive the majority of Newmont's financial performance, supported by billions in combined quarterly sales and a $1.4 billion full-year development budget explicitly targeting precious metal asset expansions. Executive leadership and organizational structures are firmly aligned with this focus, deploying dedicated underground site personnel and cross-functional operational expertise to fulfill a full-year production target of 5.3 million ounces of gold.

linked_companies.name: ROYAL GOLD INC
linked_companies.description: Acquires and manages precious metal stream and royalty interests, providing capital to mining operators in exchange for a share of future gold, silver, and other precious metal production.
linked_companies.evidence: Royal Gold's overarching business strategy relies entirely on precious metals, which recently constituted 87% of its total revenue through a 71% and 16% split between gold and silver streams. To expand this core pillar, management executes large-scale capital allocations, expanding its revolving credit facility to $2 billion to support major acquisitions like the Kansanshi and Sandstorm gold streams, alongside a $100 million commitment to secure noncore precious metals at the Warintza project. This specialized streaming and royalty framework structurally insulates the firm from direct operating cost inflation, securing its self-reported position as having the highest gold revenue concentration among its large-cap peers.

linked_companies.name: HECLA MINING CO
linked_companies.description: Operates as a primary producer of precious metals, focusing on the exploration, extraction, and development of silver and gold mining properties.
linked_companies.evidence: Hecla Mining operates exclusively as an extractor of precious metals, structurally positioned as North America's premium silver producer. The company derives approximately 87% of its total sales from this industry, with silver accounting for 73% of revenue and gold contributing the remainder through byproduct sales at sites like Greens Creek. Executive leadership directs the firm's capital directly into precious metal expansion, highlighted by a recent $40 to $50 million investment in a silver and gold recovery circuit at Greens Creek, alongside advanced drilling campaigns at the Aurora and Midas projects. This operational alignment, further reinforced by the strategic divestment of the Casa Berardi mine to concentrate on primary silver assets, dictates the company's entire business strategy and resource allocation.

linked_companies.name: COEUR MINING INC
linked_companies.description: Engages in the exploration, development, and extraction of gold and silver across multiple mining assets, directly contributing to the global supply of precious metals.
linked_companies.evidence: Coeur Mining defines its foundational corporate identity as a strictly North American-only precious metals platform, structuring its entire workforce and executive leadership around gold and silver extraction. The company recently advanced this strategy through the high-impact integration of New Gold, adding the New Afton and Rainy River mines to drive an expected 80% year-over-year increase in 2026 gold production to approximately 750,000 ounces. Coupled with output levels that place the company among the top five global silver producers, precious metals act as an absolute pure-play driver for the business, generating up to 98% of its total consolidated sales revenue.

linked_companies.name: FRESNILLO PLC
linked_companies.description: Focuses on the exploration, extraction, and processing of primary silver and gold, driving the global supply of precious metals through its active mining operations and development projects.
linked_companies.evidence: Fresnillo's business model is entirely dedicated to the extraction of precious metals, operating as the world's largest primary silver producer and Mexico's largest gold producer across eight active mines. In the first quarter of 2026, the company reported production of 11.12 million ounces of silver and 136,074 ounces of gold, maintaining a full-year gold production guidance of 500,000 to 550,000 ounces. To sustain this market leadership and support ongoing extraction, Fresnillo is investing heavily in physical infrastructure, such as the commissioning of phase XV leaching pads at Herradura and the Jarillas shaft at Saucito, alongside active workforce expansion and optimization initiatives.

themes.name: Copper Mining
themes.description: Extraction of copper ores from underground or open-pit mines, critical for electric wiring, electronics, and infrastructure applications.

linked_companies.name: FREEPORT-MCMORAN INC
linked_companies.description: Drives the global supply of copper through extensive exploration, extraction, and processing operations at major mining assets worldwide.
linked_companies.evidence: Freeport-McMoRan explicitly defines its strategic mandate and organizational structure around copper extraction, positioning itself as "America's copper champion" and a leading global supplier. This foundational focus dictates the company's capital allocation, with $4.3 billion to $4.5 billion in annual capital expenditures dedicated to major mining expansions at assets like the Bagdad, El Abra, and Grasberg Block Cave facilities. Operations across dedicated regional divisions in the U.S., South America, and Indonesia enable the company to dominate production, supplying 70% of the U.S. refined copper market. Consequently, copper mining drives the vast majority of consolidated revenues, generating a financial model so heavily leveraged to the commodity that every $0.10 per pound price fluctuation equates to a $400 million shift in annual EBITDA.

linked_companies.name: SOUTHERN COPPER CORP
linked_companies.description: Drives global copper production through extensive mining, smelting, and refining operations, supplying critical resources essential for widespread industrial and commercial applications.
linked_companies.evidence: Southern Copper Corporation operates primarily as one of the world's largest copper miners, with the metal directly generating 70.2% of the company's first-quarter 2026 revenue. To support a strategic target of achieving 1.6 million tons of annual copper production at the industry's most competitive cost, the organization is executing a $20.5 billion decade-long capital expenditure program across Peru and Mexico. This multi-billion-dollar pipeline funds specific greenfield operations such as the Tia Maria and Michiquillay developments, scaling extraction capacity by hundreds of thousands of tons while employing thousands of dedicated workers.

linked_companies.name: ANTOFAGASTA PLC
linked_companies.description: Focuses on the exploration, extraction, and processing of copper resources, operating major mining assets to supply the essential metal for global industrial applications.
linked_companies.evidence: Antofagasta's corporate structure and business model are centered strictly on copper extraction, generating approximately 80% of its total revenue through major mining operations at Los Pelambres, Centinela, Antucoya, and Zaldívar. During Q1 2026, the company produced 143,000 tonnes of copper while leveraging structural by-product credits to maintain low net cash costs of $1.08/lb, pacing toward a full-year production guidance of 650,000 to 700,000 tonnes. Furthermore, copper extraction dictates the company's central long-term investments, supported by a $3.4 billion capital expenditure budget that funds the Centinela Second Concentrator and Los Pelambres growth projects to increase overall copper production by 30%.

linked_companies.name: JIANGXI COPPER CO LTD-H
linked_companies.description: Drives the copper mining industry through extensive operations encompassing the exploration, extraction, and processing of copper resources to meet global industrial demand.
linked_companies.evidence: Jiangxi Copper Company Limited's core business identity is inextricably linked to copper mining and production, which serves as the firm's flagship product offering. The company actively manages bulk commodity inventories of copper, utilizing strict internal controls and structured hedging operations to mitigate price fluctuation risks. Additionally, its financial performance is fundamentally tied to this sector, with recent profit growth driven by year-on-year price increases of its main products and ongoing efforts to improve comprehensive resource utilization efficiency.

linked_companies.name: GLENCORE PLC
linked_companies.description: Extracts, processes, and markets copper through a global portfolio of mining assets and refining facilities, supplying critical base metals required for electrification, infrastructure development, and industrial applications.
linked_companies.evidence: Glencore's engagement with Copper Mining is driven by a strategic objective to become one of the world's largest copper producers, explicitly targeting a base copper production scale of over one million tons annually by 2026 and 1.6 million tons by 2035. This expansion is executed through a dedicated "base copper business" unit overseeing a pipeline of low-risk, capital-efficient brownfield projects situated primarily across South America and Africa. Management designates copper as "the commodity of the future," advancing approximately 1.4 million tons of incremental long-life annual production capacity through various approval phases. By structurally anchoring its metals operations around these large-scale extraction efforts, the company leverages recovered copper volumes and physical trade dislocations to propel its overarching industrial earnings and organic growth.

themes.name: Mining Exploration
themes.description: Activities to locate potential mining sites, involving surveys, drilling, and sampling to evaluate ore quality and feasibility.

linked_companies.name: IMDEX LTD
linked_companies.description: Delivers specialized drilling fluids, downhole sensors, and real-time data analytics software designed to optimize drilling operations and enhance subsurface rock knowledge across global mining exploration projects.

linked_companies.name: URANIUM ENERGY CORP
linked_companies.description: Engages in the exploration, evaluation, and development of uranium properties to advance a pipeline of mineral resource projects.
linked_companies.evidence: UEC operates as an Exploration Stage issuer primarily focused on uranium mining exploration, anchored by a regional hub-and-spoke strategy that connects satellite properties to centralized processing facilities. The company actively advances its resource evaluation pipeline, recently allocating $8.04 million over a six-month period to fund a 34,000-meter core drilling program at the Canadian Roughrider Project and extensive delineation drilling at the Sweetwater and Ludeman projects. These exploration initiatives are supported by targeted internal technical hiring and specialized regulatory positioning, notably the FAST-41 designation for the Sweetwater Project which accelerates federal permitting processes.

linked_companies.name: TMC THE METALS CO INC
linked_companies.description: Engages in deep-sea mining exploration focused on assessing and developing polymetallic nodule resources on the seafloor to supply critical metals for battery technologies.
linked_companies.evidence: The Metals Company operates as a pre-revenue deep seabed minerals developer whose business model relies on evaluating seafloor polymetallic nodules. During 2025, the organization directed $40.3 million toward exploration and evaluation expenses, funding offshore surveys, environmental baseline studies, and pilot mining tests. Subsidiaries such as NORI, TOML, and TMC USA execute this strategy by advancing International Seabed Authority exploration contracts and submitting new license applications to NOAA covering 187,017 square kilometers. Through these data collection and regulatory efforts, the company defined the world's first SEC-compliant mineral reserves for a nodule project, establishing a resource base with a $23.6 billion net present value that dictates its projected future revenue.

themes.name: Online Marketplace
themes.description: Digital platforms where buyers and sellers meet to exchange goods and services, often across vast networks, benefiting from the reach and efficiency of e-commerce.

linked_companies.name: UPWORK INC
linked_companies.description: Operates a two-sided online marketplace that connects businesses with independent professionals and agencies to facilitate freelance services and project-based work.
linked_companies.evidence: Upwork operates fundamentally as an online labor marketplace connecting clients with freelance talent, with this platform functioning as its core business identity and primary revenue engine. As of the second quarter of 2026, the company continues to optimize its ecosystem by integrating AI agents and expanding product offerings like its Business+ plan, which grew 34% quarter-over-quarter and contributed to a marketplace take rate of 19.4%. The entire executive leadership and corporate workforce are dedicated to managing and monetizing this network, which supports three million job posts annually and generates billions of dollars in Gross Services Volume. To sustain its platform capabilities, Upwork continuously directs tens of millions into quarterly research and development to build AI-native matching features, roll out dynamic fee structures, and integrate enterprise platforms such as Lifted.

linked_companies.name: STUBHUB HOLDINGS INC-CLASS A
linked_companies.description: Operates an online marketplace platform that connects buyers and sellers for the exchange of tickets to live sports, concerts, and entertainment events.
linked_companies.evidence: StubHub operates exclusively as a pure-play digital platform, with its core resale marketplace seamlessly connecting live event ticket buyers and sellers globally. Driven by an asset-light model and strong network effects, this core platform generated $2.2 billion in Gross Merchandise Sales and $446 million in total revenue during the first quarter of 2026. The company's executive leadership team directs all of its capital expenditures and internal-use software investments toward optimizing this marketplace infrastructure and expanding international liquidity. Operating as the clear market leader with an approximate 50% share of the North American secondary ticketing market, StubHub derives nearly its entire top line from transaction fees generated within this environment.

linked_companies.name: COSTAR GROUP INC
linked_companies.description: Operates extensive online real estate marketplaces that connect buyers, sellers, and renters across commercial and residential sectors through comprehensive property listings and integrated data services.
linked_companies.evidence: CoStar Group operates an extensive portfolio of digital networks—including LoopNet, Apartments.com, Homes.com, and BizBuySell—that function as multi-sided marketplaces connecting buyers, sellers, tenants, and landlords across the real estate sector. Recently, the company advanced these platforms from traditional listing sites into comprehensive transaction hubs, integrating financing and document sharing into BizBuySell to facilitate over $2 billion in enterprise value sales. These core digital platforms act as the primary delivery model for CoStar's services, collectively accounting for nearly half of the organization's total quarterly revenue. To continually scale these capabilities, the company is actively expanding its marketplace footprint into new international territories and deploying dedicated sales forces to support global transaction volumes.

linked_companies.name: ZILLOW GROUP INC - A
linked_companies.description: Operates a digital real estate platform that connects buyers, sellers, and renters with comprehensive property listings, local agents, and integrated home-related services to facilitate seamless property discovery and transactions.
linked_companies.evidence: Zillow operates fundamentally as a dual-sided digital marketplace that connects buyers, sellers, renters, and real estate professionals. Backed by a roughly $1 billion fixed cost structure to maintain its technical infrastructure, the platform drives the company's core revenue generation, managing $1.9 billion in full-year 'For Sale' transactions and $630 million in 'Rentals.' Executive leadership actively expands this ecosystem through investments in new construction networks, dedicated operational sales forces, and strategic partnerships like the Redfin syndication agreement to aggregate demand. These structural initiatives sustain a massive network effect, drawing 31 million average monthly unique visitors and hosting 2.5 million active rental listings to function as the industry's primary digital real estate hub.

linked_companies.name: AIRBNB INC-CLASS A
linked_companies.description: Operates a global peer-to-peer platform that connects hosts offering short-term stays and experiences with travelers, facilitating seamless digital transactions and driving the sharing economy within the hospitality sector.
linked_companies.evidence: Airbnb functions as a pure-play global digital marketplace spanning over 220 countries, generating its entire $12.24 billion in 2025 revenue through service fees by connecting guests with hosts. The company's core e-commerce architecture processed 533 million booked nights and experiences, resulting in $91.2 billion in Gross Booking Value for the year. To sustain and govern this two-sided network, Airbnb allocated $2.35 billion toward platform product development alongside $993 million for field operations and policy in 2025. Building on its foundation of over 5 million hosts, the company is also expanding its transactional scope by rolling out new local service categories, such as private chefs and photography, to capture localized marketplace demand.

themes.name: Artificial Intelligence
themes.description: The science of creating machines and systems capable of performing tasks that typically require human intelligence, such as learning, reasoning, and problem-solving.

linked_companies.name: MICROSOFT CORP
linked_companies.description: Drives the advancement of artificial intelligence by integrating generative AI capabilities across its enterprise software ecosystem and providing scalable cloud infrastructure to support advanced model training and deployment.
linked_companies.evidence: Microsoft's engagement with Artificial Intelligence centers on a dedicated AI business segment that recently reached a $37 billion annualized revenue run rate, expanding 123% to represent over 11% of the company's total revenue. To sustain this shift toward 'agentic' computing platforms, management is directing tens of billions in capital expenditures and increased R&D operating expenses specifically toward AI compute capacity, model training, and specialized talent acquisition. This extensive infrastructure build-out supports foundational models from its long-term OpenAI partnership, enabling the universal integration of AI tools like Copilot and Work IQ across Microsoft's consumer and enterprise software ecosystems.

linked_companies.name: NVIDIA CORP
linked_companies.description: Designs and supplies the foundational graphics processing units and software ecosystems that power artificial intelligence training and inference workloads across global data centers and accelerated computing platforms.
linked_companies.evidence: NVIDIA explicitly defines itself as a data center-scale AI infrastructure company, with its revenue growth primarily driven by Data Center AI solutions that recently accounted for over 92% of total sales. The company's core hardware and edge computing platforms are explicitly optimized for artificial intelligence, directly enabling the deployment of generative, agentic, and physical AI systems. Beyond developing foundational infrastructure, NVIDIA funds the broader global ecosystem through a $17.5 billion investment program targeting early-stage startups and AI model makers, alongside an investment partnership with OpenAI.

linked_companies.name: AMAZON.COM INC
linked_companies.description: Delivers comprehensive cloud-based artificial intelligence services, including foundational models and custom-designed machine learning chips like Trainium and Inferentia, while integrating advanced generative AI capabilities across its e-commerce platform and smart device ecosystem.
linked_companies.evidence: Amazon is directing the majority of its projected $200 billion capital expenditures toward building an end-to-end artificial intelligence ecosystem spanning custom silicon like Trainium to foundation model platforms like Bedrock. This infrastructure powers an expanding enterprise segment, with AWS artificial intelligence workloads surpassing a $15 billion annual revenue run rate by Q2 2026. The company is actively integrating generative technologies across its retail and advertising divisions, deploying over 1,000 internal applications that include the Rufus shopping assistant and Creative Agents. Amazon supplements these proprietary engineering efforts with large-scale external capital deployments, evidenced by partnerships with Anthropic and a $15 billion Series C equity investment in OpenAI.

linked_companies.name: SOUNDHOUND AI INC-A
linked_companies.description: Develops voice artificial intelligence and natural language understanding technologies that power conversational interfaces across automotive, smart device, and customer service applications.
linked_companies.evidence: As a pure-play, "AI-first" enterprise, SoundHound generates 100% of its revenues—reaching $44.2 million in Q1 2026—directly from its Voice, Generative, and Agentic AI platforms. This commercial output is driven by decades of deep tech innovation and data accumulation, anchored by the proprietary Polaris speech recognition foundation model and protected by over 240 granted patents. To further scale its conversational intelligence ecosystem, the company dedicates its entire research and development workforce to AI software advancement and recently deployed nearly $190 million to acquire AI-focused entities including Amelia Holdings and Interactions Corporation.

linked_companies.name: ALPHABET INC-CL A
linked_companies.description: Develops foundational machine learning models, specialized AI infrastructure, and advanced generative AI tools that are deeply integrated across its search, cloud computing, and consumer product ecosystems to drive broader industry innovation.
linked_companies.evidence: Alphabet's full-stack integration of Artificial Intelligence serves as the foundational driver across its entire business ecosystem, natively powering core segments including Search, Cloud, and YouTube. The recent deployment of proprietary technologies, such as Gemini 3.1 Pro models processing 16 billion tokens per minute and custom TPU 8t hardware, has propelled 800% growth in generative AI cloud solutions and secured 350 million paid AI subscriptions. Cementing this structural shift, the company increased its 2026 capital expenditure guidance to between $180 billion and $190 billion strictly for AI compute resources, accompanied by a 26% rise in research and development expenses driven directly by aggressive AI talent acquisition.

themes.name: SaaS
themes.description: Software-as-a-Service; the delivery of applications over the internet via a subscription model, allowing users access on demand without local installation.

linked_companies.name: WORKDAY INC-CLASS A
linked_companies.description: Delivers enterprise cloud applications for financial management and human resources via a Software-as-a-Service model, enabling organizations to streamline operations and manage their workforce on a unified platform.

The integration of this SaaS ecosystem is evidenced by a 97% gross revenue retention rate and a $27.3 billion total subscription backlog, which Workday continues to expand through localized platform deployments and updated consumption models like Flex Credits.

linked_companies.name: HUBSPOT INC
linked_companies.description: Provides a cloud-based customer relationship management platform delivered through a subscription model, equipping businesses with integrated marketing, sales, and service software applications.
linked_companies.evidence: Software-as-a-Service functions as the core business and delivery model for HubSpot, with the company generating 98% of its total revenue through internet-delivered software subscriptions. Utilizing seat-based and credit-based pricing formats, the company recently reported a 23% year-over-year increase in subscription revenue and a 103% net revenue retention rate across nearly 300,000 global customers. To support this overarching infrastructure, HubSpot allocates its 9,000-employee workforce and hundreds of millions of dollars in quarterly research and development spending directly toward building out its SaaS platform functionalities. Additionally, executive management anchors its competitive strategy on the interconnected nature of this platform, emphasizing that integrated SaaS workflows and governance provide operational advantages over fragmented point solutions.

linked_companies.name: CROWDSTRIKE HOLDINGS INC - A
linked_companies.description: Delivers cloud-native cybersecurity solutions through a comprehensive Software-as-a-Service platform that protects endpoints, cloud workloads, and identities across enterprise environments.
linked_companies.evidence: CrowdStrike delivers its unified security platform exclusively through a Software-as-a-Service (SaaS) subscription model, directly generating 95% of its total revenue and reaching $1.32 billion in recent quarterly subscription sales. The company allocates major capital to sustain this cloud-based delivery architecture, evidenced by a $408.3 million quarterly research and development budget and billions in ongoing cloud capacity commitments. Furthermore, CrowdStrike leverages SaaS both as its primary go-to-market engine—scaling adoption through the $1.9 billion Falcon Flex subscription framework—and as a core protection priority, utilizing products like Falcon Shield and targeted acquisitions to secure the SaaS Agentic attack surface.

linked_companies.name: ATLASSIAN CORP-CL A
linked_companies.description: Develops and delivers cloud-based collaboration, issue tracking, and project management tools through a subscription model, driving enterprise productivity and agile workflows across the software-as-a-service landscape.
linked_companies.evidence: Atlassian functions fundamentally as a Software-as-a-Service (SaaS) provider, deriving the vast majority of its revenue from cloud-hosted, seat-based subscriptions for tools like Jira and Confluence. In Q2 2026, the company's SaaS-driven cloud revenue surpassed $1.1 billion—growing 29% year-over-year—and drove total quarterly revenue to $1.8 billion. This subscription model facilitates extensive ecosystem lock-in and scale, reflected by a $4 billion Remaining Performance Obligation, a Net Retention Rate exceeding 120%, and a customer base of over 350,000. To further expand this core delivery mechanism, the company allocated $2.51 billion to research and development over a nine-month period and completed the $488.3 million acquisition of BCNY to optimize browser workflows specifically for SaaS applications.

linked_companies.name: DOCUSIGN INC
linked_companies.description: Delivers electronic signature and intelligent agreement management platforms through a cloud-based subscription model, enabling organizations to automate and digitize their document workflows.
linked_companies.evidence: DocuSign operates entirely as a Software-as-a-Service provider, consistently generating 98% of its total revenue from cloud-based subscriptions and projecting annual recurring revenue of over $3.5 billion. The company is evolving its platform monetization through the recent introduction of the IAM Platform Plan, which transitions users to a credit-based subscription pricing model tied directly to business outcomes. To support a global base of nearly 1.9 million customers, the organization aligns its infrastructure strictly with SaaS mechanics, maintaining a dedicated workforce of nearly 7,000 employees and deploying $159.5 million in quarterly research and development to expand its digital agreement capabilities.

themes.name: Generative AI & LLMs

By securing deep hardware integrations and financially backing both proprietary and open-source foundation model builders, NVIDIA structurally enables the global hyperscale transition from classical machine learning to generative AI workloads.

linked_companies.name: MICROSOFT CORP
linked_companies.description: Drives the development and commercialization of generative AI by integrating large language models into its productivity applications and providing the underlying cloud infrastructure required to train and deploy advanced AI systems.

linked_companies.name: ALPHABET INC-CL A
linked_companies.description: Develops foundational large language models and generative artificial intelligence technologies, integrating these capabilities across its search, cloud infrastructure, and software ecosystem to power advanced reasoning and automated content generation.

linked_companies.description: Provides comprehensive cloud infrastructure and platform services for generative AI, featuring custom silicon for model training and inference, managed services like Amazon Bedrock for accessing large language models, and enterprise-grade AI assistants.

linked_companies.name: COREWEAVE INC-CL A

linked_companies.evidence: CoreWeave operates as the foundational computing infrastructure for major Generative AI and large language model (LLM) platforms, powering training and inference for nine of the ten leading AI developers outside of China.
